# The Planet That Hides in Plain Sight

## Scripture
*"He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a canopy, and spreads them out like a tent to live in."* — Isaiah 40:22 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November evening, look west after sunset. Venus—the evening star—blazes there, so bright it seems almost close enough to touch. Yet appearances deceive: Venus is actually the planet that comes *nearest* to Earth, wrapped in clouds so thick we never see its surface.

There's something quietly comforting in that. The brightest light in our sky is also the closest one—hidden in plain sight, wearing a veil of clouds.

Isaiah tells us God stretches out the heavens like a tent, and yet He is not distant from what He makes. He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, yes—but He is also near. The God who flung galaxies into space bends low to listen to a whispered prayer. The One who named every star knows your name.

In this season, when the world grows dark early and the air turns cold, remember: the nearness of God is not measured by how spectacular your circumstances are. Venus shines brightest not because it is largest, but because it is near. Draw near to Him tonight. He has already drawn near to you—closer than the brightest planet, even when clouds hide His face.

## Prayer
Lord, thank You for being near—not distant or uncaring, but close enough to hear my quietest word. When I feel hidden behind clouds, remind me that Your presence is still bright. Draw me closer to You tonight, and let Your nearness be my light. Amen.
